title: God cannot create a rational creature unable to do good, but a creature can bring evil habits on itself
source_text: XXXV. Repugnat quidem divinae bonitati, justitiae, & sapientiae, ut formet creaturam aliquam intelligentem, sive rationalem, adeoque liberam, quae bene agere non possit, & quae necessitatem aliquam male agendi a Deo ipsam inditam habeat. Nec enim Deus Opt. Max. quicquam creare potest quod bonum non sit. Sed creatura quae bona a Deo producta fuit, culpa & vitio suo potest fieri mala, & eos male agendo contrahere habitus quibus ad malum ita determinetur, ut amplius bene agere non possit; voluntate, scilicet, in malo obdurata, nec valente, nisi gratiae divinae auxilio, sese ex iis laqueis extricare in quos sese ultro induit.
pass_a_gloss: It is repugnant indeed to the divine goodness, justice, & wisdom, that he should form some intelligent creature, or rational, and so free, which cannot act well, & which has some necessity of acting ill put into it by God himself. For God Most Good and Greatest cannot create anything which is not good. But a creature which was produced good by God, can by its own fault & vice become evil, & by acting ill contract those habits by which it is so determined to evil, that it can no more act well; the will, namely, being hardened in evil, nor being able, except by the help of divine grace, to extricate itself from those snares into which it has of its own accord put itself.
pass_b_english: It does clash with God's goodness, justice and wisdom for him to form an intelligent or rational, and therefore free, creature that cannot do good and has some necessity of doing evil placed in it by God himself. God, supremely good and great, cannot create anything that is not good.

But a creature that God made good can become evil by its own fault and vice. By doing evil it can acquire habits that fix it on evil so firmly that it can no longer do good. Its will is then hardened in evil and cannot, without the help of divine grace, free itself from the snares it has willingly walked into.

choices.why: Se induere in laqueos is to entangle oneself; ultro stresses that it was by choice. The English keeps both points.
rejected: put itself into of its own accord
